name: A
decision: Opposed level arms meet a long incline. Optical bars and paired serifs keep the mirrored Z legible at text sizes.

name: I
decision: The upper return levels into the same cap arm as A; its upright remains the diagnostic difference.

name: O
decision: One flowing cusp; equal-height terminals, no ragged offset seam.

name: OE
decision: A shared shoulder connects opposed posts; side spaces follow the stem class.

name: AB
decision: Return and bowl meet continuously; the bowl receives a full text-height silhouette.

name: AEB
decision: The eye has a clear counter; the two legs use the same diagonal vocabulary.

name: AG
decision: The uppercase preserves two separate opposed horns and a third detached lower staff.

name: AEG
decision: A rounded, mirrored Cyrillic-э construction: open to the right, with a bar reaching into the left bowl.

name: AD
decision: Twin serpentine strokes have matching turns and a deliberately open channel.

name: AED
decision: The cross uses balanced opposing diagonals, not unequal corner artifacts.

name: EZ
decision: Merge the upper-reaching pole and right post with a rounded cup; a lower return meets the slanted pole at mid-height.

name: AY
decision: The bowl shares the oval's counter width and the common full-height text body.

name: AEY
decision: An open head and descending hook with one clean, continuous outline.

name: AEK
decision: The two arms close into an upper bowl: a reversed P, structurally distinct from EP's open head.

name: OEK
decision: The cap arm follows I; a lower shoulder retains the two-tier distinction.

name: AL
decision: Level the bottom return, matching A's lower arm but retaining the upright.

name: AEL
decision: A Latin-like Y: two straight upper arms, one lower stem and shared cap/foot serifs.

name: ELT
decision: Two equal posts frame a smooth valley; both feet and shoulders follow the shared system.

name: EM
decision: An authored one-stroke bowl-and-leg route, like R without its upright; smoothing alone cannot derive it.

name: AN
decision: A full open bowl, like reversed C, with inward returns instead of a parenthesis.

name: AEN
decision: A single N replaces the crowded double N; no other current sign uses that construction.

name: ENT
decision: An ordinary rounded u with two upright stems; remove its three inherited dots in this proposed reform.

name: ENC
decision: Two wider bowls open the counters; keep the common upright and full stroke model.

name: ENY
decision: The middle notch becomes a waist between two open bowls, like Western 3.

name: ENG
decision: The mid-stem branch stays distinct from a bottom return without using a different cap height.

name: EP
decision: A mirrored cap arm shares the I/A family's return, without the second k arm.

name: OP
decision: Two tiers and short end stems share a standard shoulder and an open lower counter.

name: IC
decision: A Latinized mirrored Arabic 3; taper the incoming last return where it meets the unchanged straight pole.

name: EC
decision: Capital Greek-lambda construction: two straight rising legs share one pointed apex, with baseline serifs and no curved head.

name: AQ
decision: A low curling free leg distinguishes q from the upturned r; counter widths are related.

name: IQ
decision: The rounded triangle shares full height with the round bowl but preserves its pointed side.

name: OQ
decision: Retain the upright anchor construction; taper only the incoming wings at the pole.

name: AR
decision: The free leg turns upward; a related counter and equal stem keep the q/r family coherent.

name: AER
decision: Two equal shoulders meet above the stem. The stem ends at the valley, never above the roof.

name: AS
decision: One rounded upper return feeds a straight pole; IC has two returns and a third upper tip.

name: AES
decision: The minim uses the same height and stem as the rest; width comes from its two fitted side spaces.

name: ASH
decision: The oval is the reference for round counters and round-to-round spacing.

name: ESH
decision: Raise the fork's link to close its head; retain two branches and one stem, not a third upper prong.

name: AT
decision: The roof becomes an overhanging top arm; the eye moves right of the staff as one broad bowl, breaking the old symmetry.

name: AET
decision: The falling leg follows the same shoulder tension and lower counter scale as the other branched stems.

name: OT
decision: Two straight sides support an inverted u; two symmetric rounded hat prongs meet at the roof, not through it.

name: BASH
decision: An uninterrupted figure-eight route replaces the post-and-diagonal weave; two stacked counters open the waist.
